Comparison

Omarchy vs Arch Linux

Only what each project's official site says, with a source on every line.

Reviewed 2026-10-18 · independent editorial guide

Short answer

Built on Arch Linux, the Hyprland tiling window manager and the Quickshell desktop kit. Arch Linux: An independently developed x86-64 general-purpose distribution.

Side by side

OmarchyArch Linux
BaseBuilt on Arch Linux, the Hyprland tiling window manager and the Quickshell desktop kit. [omarchy.org]An independently developed x86-64 general-purpose distribution. [wiki.archlinux.org]
Release modelRolling release. New installs start on the stable channel, which follows an Omarchy Arch mirror kept one month behind the latest packages. [omarchy.org]Rolling release that aims to ship the latest stable versions of most software. [wiki.archlinux.org]
PackagesSoftware comes from Arch's core, extra and multilib repos plus the Omarchy Package Repository; the AUR is optional. Install with omarchy pkg add <package>. [omarchy.org]The pacman package manager, official repos for x86-64, and the community-operated AUR. [archlinux.org]

More about Omarchy

  • Installs from an ISO, either full-disk or into free space next to another OS. Encryption is on by default. [omarchy.org]
  • Secure Boot and/or TPM must be turned off in the BIOS to install. [omarchy.org]
  • Firewall on by default: all incoming traffic is blocked except LocalSend's port 53317, and SSH stays off until you enable it. [omarchy.org]

Sources

Omarchy facts: the Omarchy manual. Arch Linux facts: https://archlinux.org/. Checked 2026-10-18. This site is not affiliated with either project.
